subject: Packaging options for PulseCare — conditional feature swap & tier narrowing
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@pulsecare.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseCare Procurement <procurement@pulsecare.ai>
Date: 2028-08-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging question — composable vs slimline for May production

Hi Maya,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re narrowing in on the packaging question before procurement pushes the PO through. A couple of clarifying items from our side:

- We run two main workloads: conversational triage (short chats, high QPS) and batch note embedding (large daily jobs). The triage workload values latency, the embedding job values unit cost.
- Procurement asked whether we can start on the composable plan and narrow to a slimline, lower-feature plan after 3 months if usage patterns favor the embedding job. Are there clean downgrade paths that don’t require an amendment or long lead time?
- We also want to understand conditional feature swaps — specifically, can we remove streaming/function-calls from the primary tier and keep it for a smaller seat pool?

Can you send a concise option set (pricing delta, seat implications, any credits or migration fees) so we can present to finance?

Thanks,
Elena
--
Elena Rossi
Head of ML Ops, PulseCare

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@pulsecare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-30T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — composable vs slimline for May production

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a short usage snapshot template and a slimline vs composable comparison PDF (attached). High-level options below:

1) Start Composable (recommended short-term)
- Pricing: standard composable rate (see PDF)
- Downgrade path: 90-day notice to move to Slimline; automatic prorate for unused committed credits; no migration fee if you accept standard SLA window.
- Feature swap: streaming/function-calls can be gated per-seat; we can keep streaming enabled for a 10-seat pool and disable on the rest.

2) Start Slimline with Add-on Burst
- Pricing: lower base, add-on burst at higher per-token during triage spikes
- Downgrade/upgrade: immediate via console (no contract change) but burst capacity billed separately

3) Pilot Hybrid (3 months)
- We can provision a small dedicated slimline pool for embeddings and leave composable for triage. After 90 days we’ll provide a migration playbook and an expected cost delta.

Next steps I suggest: you complete the usage snapshot (attached csv) and I’ll run a short model->workload mapping to give exact delta numbers. Ben / Kimberly — can you confirm any standard credit for switches in the first 180 days?

Best,
Maya
Product Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pulsecare-usage-snapshot.csv, redwood-slimline-comparison.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena@pulsecare.ai>
Date: 2028-08-30T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — composable vs slimline for May production

Thanks Maya — quick commercial note to include in the packet:

- For deals moving to production within 60 days we can offer a one-time migration credit equal to 10% of the first quarter’s committed spend to cover rollout costs (DEV/SE time). That credit applies if the customer executes the downgrade/upgrade within the first 180 days without expanded feature requests beyond what we scoped.
- If procurement wants downgrade flexibility without change orders, we can include a standard amendment clause: 90-day notice, automated console flow, and no early termination fee.

I’ll draft a short commercial summary and send it once we have the usage numbers. Ben

From: Elena Rossi <elena@pulsecare.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseCare Procurement <procurement@pulsecare.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-31T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — composable vs slimline for May production

Maya — attaching the filled snapshot (see attached). Our preferences:

- We prefer Pilot Hybrid (option 3) if the credit and migration commitments are formalized.
- We need the streaming/function-call gating on a 15-seat pool and slimline embedding pool at lower throughput but higher batch efficiency.
- Procurement asks for a written note that moving from composable -> slimline will not require a full contract renegotiation and that the 10% migration credit will be applied to Q1 invoice after the switch.

Can you confirm and send the proposal? If we can get a signed DocuSign within 7 business days, procurement will greenlight the PO.

On Tue, Aug 30, 2028 at 11:02 AM Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a short usage snapshot...

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, PulseCare Procurement <procurement@pulsecare.ai>
Date: 2028-08-31T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — composable vs slimline for May production

Elena — thanks for the snapshot and the clarity. Summary of proposal below (I’ve also attached a one-page commercial summary):

Proposal summary (Pilot Hybrid)
- Pilot term: 3 months; start on composable for triage + dedicated slimline pool for embeddings
- Downgrade path: 90-day notice from the date you trigger the migration flow; automatic prorate on credits; no migration fee if scope matches pilot; amendment language included in DocuSign.
- Feature gating: streaming/function-calls kept only on the 15-seat triage pool (we’ll show console settings during onboarding).
- Commercials: committed quarterly spend: $120k (estimated based on your snapshot); one-time migration credit: 10% of first quarter ($12k) applied after successful migration; effective net first-quarter spend: $108k.

Ask from PulseCare: please confirm acceptance of pilot terms and procurement info (billing contact and legal contact). Once you confirm I’ll send the DocuSign with the amendment clause and the commercial summary.

Next steps:
- Elena / Procurement: confirm acceptance and provide billing/legal contacts (by EOD Fri to meet your 7 business day window)
- Ben / Kimberly: I’ve attached the proposed-commercial-summary-pulsecare.xlsx — Ben will input the final line-item pricing and push the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-commercial-summary-pulsecare.xlsx
